source_passages.statement_original:
We use the conventions $\langle u,v angle=\sum_i
\overline{u_i}v_i$ for the complex inner product, $\|u\|$ for the (real or complex) $\ell_2$-norm, $\|M\|$ for the $\ell_2 	o \ell_2$ operator norm for matrices, and $\mathbf{i}=\sqrt{-1}$ for the imaginary unit.

For a measure space $(X,\mu)$, $L_2(X,\mathbb{C})$ is the $L_2$-space of functions $f:X 	o \mathbb{C}$ with inner-product $\int_X
\overline{f(x)}g(x)\mu(\mathrm{d}x)$. We write $L_2(X)=L_2(X,\mathbb{R})$ for the analogous $L_2$-space of real-valued functions. $\mathcal{S}^1$ and $\mathcal{S}^2$ are the unit circle and unit sphere.

For differentiable $f:\mathbb{R}^d 	o \mathbb{R}^k$, $\mathrm{d}f(x) \in \mathbb{R}^{k 	imes d}$ is its derivative or Jacobian at $x$. For twice-differentiable $f:\mathbb{R}^d 	o \mathbb{R}$, $
abla f(x)=\mathrm{d}f(x)^	op \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is its gradient, and $
abla^2 f(x) \in \mathbb{R}^{d 	imes d}$ is its Hessian. We will write $\mathrm{d}_x,
abla_x,
abla_x^2$ to clarify that the variable of differentiation is $x$. For a subset of coordinates $y$, we write $
abla_y f(x)$ and $
abla_y^2 f(x)$ as the components of this gradient and Hessian in $y$.

For a smooth manifold $\mathcal{M}$ and twice-differentiable $f:\mathcal{M} 	o \mathbb{R}$, we write $
abla f(x)|_{\mathcal{M}}$ and $
abla^2 f(x)|_{\mathcal{M}}$ for its gradient and Hessian evaluated in any choice of local chart at $x \in \mathcal{M}$. We will often not make the choice of chart explicit when referring to properties of $
abla f(x)|_{\mathcal{M}}$ and $
abla^2 f(x)|_{\mathcal{M}}$ that do not depend on the specific choice of chart.

source_passages.source_heading: Section 2.2 — tensor inner product and norm
source_passages.statement_original: We denote by $\langle \cdot,\cdot \rangle$ the Euclidean inner-product in the vectorization of these tensor spaces $\mathbb{R}^{d \times \ldots \times d}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{\tilde{d}\times \ldots \times \tilde{d}}$, and by $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2$ the corresponding squared Euclidean norm.

evidence.location: Last paragraph of Section 2.2 before Theorem 2.2

ambient_notions: Compact orthogonal and special orthogonal groups, Haar integration, polynomial rings and generated subalgebras.
Analytic maps, Lebesgue-null exceptional sets, smooth manifolds, Hessian spectra and constant-rank derivatives.
Euclidean tensor products and vectorization, Gaussian laws, white noise, finite orthonormal expansions.
The sin-theta distance between subspaces and Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse are standard ambient notions named in Theorem 2.7; the theorem itself binds V_k and W_k.
Real spherical harmonics, complex spherical harmonics and inverse Fourier transforms are named locally, but the paper-specific basis and phase conventions deferred to appendices remain unresolved.
